headline: Jake Tapper: Trump’s Outside Advisers Pushing For Martial Law Takeover Of Midterms
trending_claim: Outside advisers to Trump, including attorney Peter Tickton, are urging him to take federal control of the 2026 midterms — including by declaring martial law on or around Election Day — as reported by The Atlantic and covered in a CNN segment by Jake Tapper.
rating_explained: The Atlantic's reporting by Yvonne Wingett Sanchez and Michael Scherer is the basis: Election Law Blog quotes it at length, with attorney Peter Ticktin (the Atlantic's spelling; Crooks and Liars renders it 'Tickton') laying out three scenarios for the fall, the last being that Trump 'tries to declare martial law on or around November 3' — 'Either martial law, or step aside.' Baller Alert, summarizing the same reporting, confirms CNN's Jake Tapper covered the piece Thursday on The Lead. The Atlantic's piece itself is careful to frame this as pressure from outside advisers: it reports a White House official saying Ticktin, Wayne Allyn Root and Tina Peters 'play no role in election policy,' and a DOJ spokesperson saying there are no such plans. The trending claim faithfully reports what The Atlantic reported and that Tapper covered it, without asserting Trump has decided to act, so the claim stands as accurate.

sources.name: Election Law Blog (quoting The Atlantic)
Baller Alert

trending_context: Front-page lead on Crooks and Liars' 'The Latest' on Sep 26–27, driven by The Atlantic's reporting and Jake Tapper's CNN segment.

headline: SCOTUS Again Blocks Missouri’s Gerrymandered Congressional Map
trending_claim: In a unanimous unsigned decision, the Supreme Court ordered Missouri to use the 2022 congressional map — not the legislature's 2025 gerrymandered map — for the 2026 election, ruling that as a matter of state law the 2022 map must be used.
rating_explained: The Associated Press reported on September 26, 2026 that the Supreme Court, in an unsigned opinion with 'no noted dissents,' halted the 8th Circuit ruling and let stand the Missouri Supreme Court's decision, quoting the high court: 'The District Court and Court of Appeals should not enjoin or otherwise prohibit the use of the 2022 map in the 2026 congressional election in Missouri.' The Missouri Independent's original reporting (by Rudi Keller) describes it as 'a unanimous decision' and quotes the ruling verbatim: 'In short, as a matter of state law, the 2022 map — not the 2025 map — must be used in the 2026 congressional election.' AP adds the context that the 2025 map was used in the August primaries and targeted Rep. Emanuel Cleaver's district. Every element of the trending claim — unanimous, unsigned, 2022 map for 2026, as a matter of state law — matches the named sources exactly.

sources.name: Associated Press (via WCIA)
Missouri Independent (via The Pitch KC)

trending_context: Leading Crooks and Liars on Sep 26 (via the Missouri Independent), capping three weeks of court fights that changed the map in place five times.

headline: US Amb. To China Insists Trump Got Assurances From Xi On Iran

rating_explained: Reuters reported September 25–26, 2026 that Perdue said on CNBC that Trump reiterated to Xi that direct or indirect support for Iran was 'totally unacceptable,' and told Fox News' 'America's Newsroom' when asked whether China would stop assisting Iran: 'That's what the commitment is. They assured us yesterday they're not doing that.' The AP's summit wrap confirms the broader framing: the visit was 'heavy on pomp and light on substance' with 'no major breakthroughs,' and the CBS News piece 'Trump-Xi visit to Washington wraps up with few achievements announced' is confirmed as published September 25, 2026. One material caveat: Reuters also reported that a senior Iranian official told the wire Chinese officials assured Iran that Beijing would not limit its economic, political or military ties with Tehran under US pressure — directly contradicting Perdue's claimed assurance. The trending claim accurately recounts what Perdue said and the CBS contrast, so it is accurate; whether Beijing's assurance is real is disputed, not established.

headline: White House Claim of $250 Billion in Fraud Questionable
trending_claim: The New York Times' Linda Qiu found the White House fraud task force's ledger — touted by JD Vance as $250 billion in fraud found since he became 'fraud czar' — is difficult to verify, includes cases from the Biden administration, and leans on unverified or prematurely counted allegations.
rating_explained: The NYT findings as published are corroborated on every checkable point. An independent analysis by the Washington Sun (republished by Opera News) confirms Vance told an RNC crowd in April that 'we found $250 billion of fraud just since the president made me the fraud czar,' yet the ledger dates its $245.7 billion figure to January 2025 — months before Vance took the role — and the White House would not say which timeframe is correct, establishing the figure is genuinely difficult to verify. The same analysis documents the ledger's Biden-era entries: the Small Business Administration's $22.2 billion in flagged fraudulent loans was actually identified during the Biden administration, and a 'top ten' enforcement entry touting four captured fugitives includes three charged in 2019 and 2024, before this administration took office. Even the administration-friendly WLT Report confirms the shifting headline numbers — Vance's Sept 25 update claims $260.7B 'uncovered' since January 2025, $72B stopped and $58.9B recovered — and concedes 'uncovered' means estimated suspicious payments flagged for examination, not court judgments, which matches the NYT's language about unverifiable or prematurely counted allegations quoted by PoliticalWire. One caveat: the NYT piece itself is paywalled, so I verified its content through published excerpts plus independent corroboration. Because the claim accurately describes the NYT's findings and those findings are independently substantiated, the verdict is accurate.

WLT Report — Trump White House Drops Stunning New Fraud Ledger (Sept 25, 2026)

headline: Trump allies could use midterms ‘counting window’ to disrupt results, experts warn
trending_claim: Election experts including former officials Caitlin Durkovich, Larry Norden and Ben Hovland warn the Trump administration could exploit the post-election 'counting window' — using claims of foreign interference to seize equipment or ballots and amplify unfounded fraud allegations to challenge midterm results.

Memeorandum's aggregator page lists it as 'Trump allies could use midterms counting window to disrupt results, experts warn (George Chidi/The Guardian),' and PoliticalWire's own Sept 27 coverage links directly to theguardian.com, confirming the original Guardian piece exists with this headline and author; the original Guardian URL was not directly fetchable in this environment. I opened the provided mirror (thebullpost.press) and found its text consistent with the attributed Guardian piece, including the direct quotes, so the mirror URL is retained as a confirmed verbatim carrier. The substance checks out: the piece quotes former deputy homeland security adviser Caitlin Durkovich telling a Brennan Center for Justice briefing that the administration could 'use the claim of foreign interference at the end of voting days to either seize equipment or to seize ballots, whether they're legally justified to do so or not,' quotes Brennan Center's Larry Norden ('This is the biggest threat right now') and former EAC chair Ben Hovland (on the administration's 'narrative of fraud' and 'live ballots'). This is a warnings story, and the claim's 'could' framing is its honest frame: the experts are predicting future risk, not asserting past facts, and it is accurate that they issued these warnings.

headline: Everything we know about Brian Cole, the DC pipe bombing suspect
trending_claim: Attorney General Pam Bondi asserts the five-year pipe-bomb investigation 'languished' under Biden for four years, that the FBI had all the needed evidence the whole time, and that the Trump DOJ cracked the case through diligent police work — a claim now being paired on the right with Tucker Carlson's interview of Cole's parents, who say he was framed.
rating_explained: The arrest record is established: Brian Cole Jr. was arrested Dec 4, 2025, and on July 7, 2026 Judge Amir Ali denied his motion to dismiss, ruling Trump's Jan 6 pardons do not cover him because he 'had not been convicted of the conduct at issue when the President issued the pardon' and was not charged until nearly a year after the proclamation (WSYR/iHeart court coverage). Bondi did make the 'languished' remark — 'This case languished. It sat there for four years collecting dust' — but on Fox & Friends on Dec 5, 2025, not this weekend; it is being re-amplified now alongside Tucker Carlson's Sept 17, 2026 interview of Cole's parents, who say their son was framed (confirmed by WLT Report quoting Carlson's X post). The factual core of Bondi's claim comes from Deputy FBI Director Dan Bongino himself: a fresh team assigned about two months before the arrest 'scoured existing evidence,' and the key evidence — credit-card purchases of bomb components, cell-phone and vehicle activity from Jan 5 — was 'gathered under the previous administration' (RealClearInvestigations, citing AP). But the blanket claim of four years of inaction is contradicted by the on-the-record record: former director Wray testified under oath the FBI was 'aggressively investigating' with a dedicated team, and the FBI made repeated public appeals and doubled its reward — though a January 2025 House GOP report alleged resources were diverted as early as February 2021. So the arrest is real and the evidence-predated-the-new-team claim is supported by the FBI's own deputy director, but 'no one did anything for four years' is an unverifiable characterization with named contradictory evidence on the record — hence mixed. The pardon fight is also real: the motion was denied, trial is set for February 2027.

sources.name: RealClearInvestigations (via TIPP Insights) — DC Pipe Bomb Arrest Raises Questions About Christopher Wray's FBI (Dec 12, 2025)
570 WSYR / iHeart — Judge Rules Accused Jan. 6 Pipe Bomber Not Covered By Trump Pardons (July 7, 2026)
WLT Report — Mother of Accused J6 Pipe-Bomb Suspect Interview (Sept 17, 2026)

headline: Trump to set new fuel economy standards and undo Biden-era 'EV mandate'

rating_explained: The Washington Examiner quotes Trump's Saturday-night announcement verbatim: he approved new fuel-economy standards that 'TERMINATE' Biden's 'ridiculous EV Mandate,' said the old rules 'cost our Great Auto Manufacturers $Billions,' promised 'LOWER PRICES, saving families thousands,' and declared 'Plants are coming back, and Jobs are returning, to Michigan, Ohio, Indiana, South Carolina,' with Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy confirming the rule lands Monday. The claim faithfully describes the announcement, so the verdict is accurate.

headline: Senate Rejects Latest Bid to Curb Trump's Iran War Powers
trending_claim: The Senate defeated the Iran war powers resolution 50-49 on Thursday: four Republicans (Rand Paul, Susan Collins, Lisa Murkowski, Thom Tillis) voted for it, Democrat John Fetterman was the lone Democrat voting against it, and the measure died because it needed 51 votes.
rating_explained: Newsmax asserts the Senate rejected the Iran war powers resolution 50-49 on Thursday, with four named Republicans voting for it and Fetterman as the lone Democratic no vote. NPR (via WAMC) confirms the resolution failed 49 to 50 and names the same four Republicans — Susan Collins, Lisa Murkowski, Rand Paul, Thom Tillis — as voting with Democrats, with Pennsylvania Sen. John Fetterman 'the lone Democrat to vote no.' Reuters (via SRN News) independently confirms the identical 50-49 tally, the same four Republican yes votes, and Fetterman as the single Democrat voting against. The only flaw is the claim's 'needed 51 votes' explanation: because 99 of 100 senators voted, a simple majority of 50 would have sufficed for passage, so the measure actually fell one yes vote short of 50, not 51. The vote count, the four Republican names, and Fetterman's unique Democratic opposition are all confirmed by two wire outlets; only the threshold number is slightly off.

headline: Facing a barrage of Republican anti-trans ads, some Democrats are changing how they respond
trending_claim: Democrats in competitive midterms — including James Talarico (TX Senate), Rep. Marcy Kaptur (OH), and Amy Acton (OH governor) — are now publicly opposing trans athletes in girls' sports or trans ideology after GOP advertisers spent more than $60 million on 190+ transgender-focused TV ads this year, per AdImpact.
rating_explained: The CNN piece (the R07 article) asserts that Democrats including James Talarico, Marcy Kaptur, and Amy Acton have taken public positions opposing trans athletes in girls' sports or trans 'ideology,' in the context of AdImpact data showing GOP advertisers spent over $60 million on 190+ transgender-referencing TV ads this year. The CNN wire copy (via KION) confirms each element verbatim: Talarico told Fox News he would 'oppose trans athletes playing in girls' sports if it risks safety or fairness'; Kaptur aired ads saying she 'voted with Republicans to keep transgender ideology out of schools,' prompting Equality Ohio to downgrade her from B to D; Acton was downgraded from A to B after saying in June she does 'not support boys playing in girls' sports'; and 'according to data from AdImpact, GOP advertisers spent more than $60 million airing more than 190 TV ads that reference transgender policies since the start of the year.' Reuters (via Northland News Radio) independently corroborates the broader ad-blitz premise, reporting Republican-aligned groups attacking Sherrod Brown over transgender rights in Ohio and citing AdImpact on the heavy spending in that race. Every checkable claim in the trending claim is confirmed by named outlets.
